item.title: Noem, top DHS officials to be deposed in FEMA staffing cut lawsuit
item.description: The order comes after a DoJ lawyer contradicted a top FEMA official’s statement about whether DHS made the final call on staffing cuts.

item.title: Lawsuit contends Schedule Policy/Career exceeds presidential authority
item.description: An expanded lawsuit comes just days ahead of President Donald Trump’s anticipated finalization of federal employee transfers into Schedule Policy/Career.

item.title: These 2 recent cases confirm DOJ is escalating cyber enforcement
item.description: "The trend here is focused on misrepresentations and material noncompliance with cybersecurity obligations," rather than data breaches, Lance Taubin said.

item.title: New bill would push agencies toward shared services for federal lending programs
item.description: Legislation introduced in both houses of Congress on Wednesday would require the government to create a new front door for loans at Lending.gov.

item.title: OPM wants agencies to prioritize employees’ performance, not tenure, during RIFs
item.description: The Trump administration's proposal to prioritize performance in RIFs comes after OPM teed up plans to limit high performance ratings for federal employees.

item.title: Army overhauls direct commissioning process to bring in civilian tech experts faster
item.description: "We're focused on folks coming in at the lieutenant, captain level to help us in the technical areas in our operational units,” Brig. Gen. Gregory Johnson said.

item.title: Building a resilient federal government takes partnerships
item.description: Gaddafi Ismail, the president of De Lune Corp., explains why contractors are an important piece in keeping the federal mission moving when disruption hits.

item.title: Is SDA getting ahead of itself on missile-warning satellites?
item.description: "When you think about doing the hard things that SDA is charged with doing here, you have to recognize that it's going to take time," Jon Ludwigson said.

item.title: US issues first commercial construction permit for a nuclear reactor in years to a Wyoming project
item.description: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission has issued its first construction permit for a commercial nuclear reactor in eight years. The commission granted the permit Wednesday for a Bill Gates-backed company to build a sodium-cooled nuclear reactor in western Wyoming. The company filed for the permit in 2024. item.description: "The rules for budget reconciliation are fairly straightforward, but it requires a trifecta to pull off," John Ferrari said.
